data.content_ref: inline:The problem demands identifying the 'single mechanism' that best explains why the nocturnal UHI gap is larger in some cities than others. The target instead commits to street-canyon radiative-trap geometry as the cross-city modulator, which is scientifically incomplete: it omits the dominant cross-city driver—anthropogenic heat release—which is a required term in any cross-city energy-balance commitment and is explicitly listed in the cross-city modulator predicate ('population'). The target even provides its own overturn condition that empirical studies show nocturnal UHI intensity is uncorrelated with sky view factor after controlling for thermal mass and anthropogenic heat, undermining radiative trapping as the single best mechanism.
